subject: Architecture
title: Mycelium: Building with Mushroom Roots
description: Learn Mycelium: Building with Mushroom Roots in one minute.

hook.text: Mushroom roots can be grown into building blocks in just five days — no kiln, no factory needed.

buildup.text: Mycelium grows through agricultural waste, binding it into solid panels that insulate and resist fire.

discovery.text: At the end of a building's life, mycelium blocks can be composted — they return to soil in weeks.

twist.text: The MoMA PS1 gallery displayed a tower of mycelium bricks — grown, exhibited, and composted in one summer.

climax.text: Companies like Ecovative are scaling mycelium production for packaging, insulation, and structural panels.

punchline.text: Grow your walls. Compost them when done. Repeat forever.

quiz.question: How long does it take to grow mycelium building blocks?

details.summary: Mycelium — the root network of fungi — can be grown into building panels, bricks, and insulation by feeding it agricultural waste in molds. The resulting material is lightweight, fire-resistant, and compostable.
details.whyItMatters: Mycelium materials grow rather than being manufactured, using agricultural waste as feedstock with almost no energy input. They offer a genuinely circular construction material that can be composted at end of life rather than sent to landfill.
takeaways: Fungi root networks are grown into panels, bricks, and insulation
Made from agricultural waste with minimal energy input
Compostable at end of life for truly circular construction

faq.question: How strong are mycelium building materials?
faq.answer: Current mycelium panels have compressive strengths comparable to polystyrene foam — suitable for insulation and non-load-bearing partitions, not structural use.

faq.question: Are mycelium buildings commercially available?
faq.answer: Companies like Ecovative Design produce mycelium insulation and packaging commercially. Building-scale applications remain mostly experimental, with pavilions and installations demonstrating the technology.
